Mesa — starters and five more

Read-only evaluation. The first five alternatives add a Type absent from the starter set first, then sort alphabetically; this is a preview, not a stored rank. WSRS-TSO will use actual curated Type coverage. No resource is marked Curated here. Items needing resolution stay in the administrator list.

Addiction

Combine urgent adult access, local medication and treatment options, adolescent and women-focused care, different mutual-support choices, family help, harm reduction and court-related treatment. Preserve reserve alternatives for access, preference and capacity.

Starter set

Community Bridges, Inc. · Mesa crisis stabilization, withdrawal management and treatment access

Adult crisis assessment, withdrawal/stabilization and treatment routing with access regardless of ability to pay.

Adult crisis criteria and clinical triage apply; the entry point does not guarantee a residential bed.

New Hope Behavioral Health Center — OTP/SUD Treatment Clinic

Mesa opioid medication treatment with local intake and public-funding routes.

Medication, dosing, payer and available funding require assessment; check the specific pregnancy or age-related pathway.

Unhooked Recovery - Mesa Detox, Residential, and Outpatient Services

Local detox, residential and outpatient options with separately labeled intake contacts.

Different levels of care use different locations and contacts; admission, payment and space must be confirmed.

Arizona Women's Recovery Center - Women's Outpatient Treatment and Supportive Housing

Women-centered outpatient care and treatment-linked housing/family supports.

Housing is tied to treatment; Phoenix travel, clinical fit, funding and openings matter.

Adolescent Substance Abuse Program (ASAP) - Mesa Adolescent IOP

Mesa adolescent outpatient substance-use treatment with parent involvement.

For ages 12–18 with parent participation; in-person counselling only, without detox or residential care.

Alcoholics Anonymous · East Valley Intergroup

Free local alcohol-recovery mutual support and helpline.

Peer support cannot manage dangerous withdrawal or replace clinical treatment.

SMART Recovery - Mesa Meetings and Family & Friends Meeting Finder

Alternative self-management mutual support with online access and family options.

Use current meeting listings; this is mutual support, not a clinic or crisis service.

East Valley Al-Anon

Local support for family/friends affected by another person's drinking.

For people affected by another person’s drinking; meeting times and language options vary.

Shot in the Dark - Mesa Harm-Reduction Site

Mesa low-barrier overdose-prevention/harm-reduction supply access.

Text for current Mesa location details; the street address is intentionally not public.

SAGE Counseling, Inc. - City of Mesa Diversion Treatment Program

Local court/diversion-related substance-use education and outpatient treatment.

Assessment, court paperwork, costs and payer rules depend on the programme.

Gaps: No starter guarantees an available residential bed, transportation or payment. Pregnancy-specific inpatient care, long-term recovery housing and additional culturally specific pathways remain important reserve choices.

Disability

A ten-resource starting set balances system entry and care funding with employment, family guidance, equipment, rights, sensory access and a local direct-service provider. Selections reflect complementary client pathways and practical access, not a claim that these providers are superior. Numerous other providers remain available so a curator can choose alternatives that fit a person’s needs and avoid concentrating referrals unnecessarily.

Starter set

Ability360 - Center for Independent Living Services and Information & Referral

Provides a cross-disability starting point for independent-living questions, local information and help navigating community supports.

Individual services and eligibility differ; this is not a guarantee of funded personal care or an immediate provider placement.

AHCCCS - Arizona Long Term Care System (ALTCS)

Provides the long-term-care coverage pathway that can make in-home or residential support affordable for qualifying people.

Financial and medical criteria apply, and evaluation takes time. An application is not an immediate care placement.

Encircle Families - Family Support and Parent-to-Parent Disability Navigation

Gives families no-cost guidance, parent connections and help navigating a child’s disability, school and health systems.

Program scope and availability vary. Navigation and mentoring do not replace a school evaluation, clinical treatment or legal representation.

AzTAP Assistive Technology Services and AzLAT Loans

Lets people explore assistive technology through assessment, demonstrations, trials, reuse and possible financing.

Equipment inventory and loan terms vary. AzLAT financing must be repaid; school-only lending has a separate professional request process.

Disability Rights Arizona - protection and advocacy legal services

Provides disability-rights resources and an intake route for legal barriers involving services, education, access or discrimination.

Cases are selected according to priorities and capacity. The published notice pauses new intake until September 28, 2026 at 8 a.m.; recheck before referral.

Foundation for Blind Children · Blind and Low-Vision Services

Adds specialized vision-loss guidance, training and technology support for children, adults and older adults.

Confirm the correct program, funding and location. The organization’s name does not mean that only children qualify.

Valley Center of the Deaf - Deaf, DeafBlind, and Hard-of-Hearing Independent Living Services

Adds a practical deaf and DeafBlind service pathway for communication access, independent living and support navigation.

Eligibility, equipment and interpreting services have separate conditions. Confirm the appropriate program and current communication contact.

Copa Health — Disability living, in-home, day and employment supports

Adds a Mesa provider with concrete day, home, community-living and employment supports after the appropriate authorization is arranged.

DDD, VR, behavioral-health or other payer authorization and openings vary by program. The administrative location is not a walk-in residential placement.

DES Division of Developmental Disabilities — eligibility and member supports

Adds the eligibility and support-coordination route for developmental-disability services, connecting families to authorized home, day, respite and employment supports.

DDD eligibility and programme authorization apply; many funded supports also require ALTCS, and neither diagnosis nor enrollment guarantees a particular service.

Arizona Department of Economic Security · Vocational Rehabilitation (VR)

Adds an individualized public employment pathway for people whose disability makes finding or keeping work difficult.

Eligibility and an approved employment plan govern training, equipment and travel support; this is not a general tuition or transportation benefit.

Gaps: The set does not individually cover every diagnosis, SSA cash-benefit application, caregiver respite provider, accessible-transport option, home-modification fund, recreation activity or residential budget. The reserve includes these pathways and additional direct providers; all services remain subject to their own eligibility, authorization and capacity.

Domestic Violence

Start with three independent shelter providers spread across the Valley, alongside mobile advocacy, trauma care, civil legal help, court access, escape assistance,always-available support and address privacy. This spreads referrals while covering materially different needs. It is a curation starting set, not a claim these providers fit every survivor.

Starter set

Catholic Charities Community Services Arizona - My Sisters' Place Domestic Violence Shelter

Establish an East Valley shelter with a direct 24-hour hotline, free services and explicit access for individuals, families, men and women.

Beds require safety/intake screening; the public Catholic Charities office is not the confidential shelter.

Chicanos Por La Causa - De Colores Domestic and Sexual Violence Services

Adds a separate bilingual shelter and community advocacy provider, with direct nonshelter access and pet support.

Confirm shelter openings, language/animal needs and whether the public community site is the appropriate appointment location.

New Life Center - Shelter and Survivor Advocacy

Adds West Valley shelter capacity through a third provider, plus pet accommodation, mobile support and distinct sexual-assault services.

Shelter, Sunshine services and Fresh Start outreach have separate contacts/access rules; none guarantees immediate placement.

Eve's Place Community Services - Mobile Advocacy Program

Provides mobile advocacy, court support and practical connections for survivors who are not entering a shelter.

Arrange a safe contact and meeting; the public mailing suite is not a walk-in service location.

La Frontera EMPACT-Suicide Prevention Center - Trauma Healing Services

Provides free trauma therapy and 24-hour survivor intake, including local sites and Maricopa telehealth, rather than relying only on shelter-based counseling.

Ask which therapy or mobile service fits and when it is available; hotline availability does not guarantee an immediate appointment.

Community Legal Services - Civil Legal Aid and MesaCAN Intake

Adds civil legal screening for family-law, housing and other survivor-related problems, with potentially broader remedies than protective-order paperwork alone.

Income, funding, case type and capacity apply; immigration-status exceptions need screening and representation is not automatic.

Mesa Municipal Court - Protective Order Filing and Emergency Order Pathway

Provides an actual local court filing/hearing route after AZPOINT preparation, making the protective-order process actionable.

Court jurisdiction and pending family cases affect where to file; an order needs judicial review and service, and is not a safety guarantee.

Control Alt Delete - One-Time Emergency Escape Assistance

Adds possible help with immediate escape costs, transportation or temporary arrangements that safety planning alone cannot supply.

An advocate must refer; survivors cannot self-refer and funding or hotel help is never guaranteed.

National Domestic Violence Hotline - 24/7 Confidential Hotline, Chat and Text

Adds round-the-clock national advocacy and safety planning when local offices are closed or another confidential contact is needed.

It does not itself supply local shelter beds or financial aid; use a device and contact method the survivor considers safe.

Arizona Secretary of State - Address Confidentiality Program

Adds a specific privacy safeguard: substitute-address use and eligible mail forwarding for survivors moving to a confidential location.

Eligibility includes moving plans/recent move, documentation and an Application Assistant; the address cannot be used before approval.

Gaps: Keep Deaf/ASL, Native/tribal, LGBTQ-specific, veteran/military, campus, older-adult, child-specific, immigration and longer-term housing alternatives searchable in the reserve. The selected shelter providers have different access and pet arrangements; no bed availability is guaranteed.

Education

Balances adult learning, language, technology, technical careers, college costs, youth transition, tutoring and consequential access barriers. Uses multiple providers and avoids treating annual closed scholarship applications as immediate funding.

Starter set

Mesa Public Schools Community Education · Mesa Adult Education and Family Literacy

Provides a local adult-education entry point for foundational skills, English and high-school-equivalency goals.

Enrollment, testing, lawful-presence rules and current class schedules must be checked for the chosen course.

Friendly House · Adult Education and Workforce Development

Adds a second community adult-learning provider with English and workforce-linked instruction, spreading referrals beyond one school system.

Travel to Phoenix and in-person orientation/testing may be needed even for hybrid classes.

Provides approachable library learning tools and digital instruction for clients beginning with basic technology or conversation skills.

Branch schedules vary, and some online products require a library card.

Helps clients turn college plans into an application and funding plan rather than assuming a scholarship will cover the bill.

Aid has program-specific eligibility and deadlines; advice does not guarantee funding.

Adds a local hands-on technical-training route for people seeking a vocational credential.

Adult technical programs have separate admission requirements and fees; they are not the free adult-basic-education program.

Each program has its own age, school and participation requirements.

Documentation and advance processing are needed; accommodations are determined individually.

Requires an MCLD account; live tutor subjects and hours vary.

Usually ages 16–24 with income, status, background and readiness requirements; intake and residential arrangements require confirmation.

Connects families and unaccompanied youth to the school liaison when housing instability threatens enrollment or attendance.

A school-support route, not shelter placement; the local liaison assesses the student’s circumstances.

Gaps: Specialized refugee and Native American programs, foster-youth aid, apprenticeships, parent education and business learning remain valuable reserve expansions. Availability, travel, schedules and individual eligibility still govern referrals.

Financial Assistance

Combine local emergency help, recurring public benefits, income after job loss, financial counseling, tax preparation, benefit appeals, medical-bill relief and two consequential specialist pathways. Several public benefits necessarily share a government administrator; other options spread referrals across distinct community providers.

Starter set

A New Leaf / MesaCAN - Rent, Mortgage, and Utility Assistance

Provides Mesa’s local rent, mortgage and utility screening route, with separate instructions for each need.

Appointments and funds are limited; rental requests require the published first-Thursday phone window.

Health-e-Arizona Plus — benefits applications, notices and records

Provides one online route to screen or apply for nutrition, cash and health benefits, with community-assistor options.

Each benefit has separate eligibility and document rules; an application is not approval or immediate money.

Social Security Administration - SSI/SSDI Disability Income Application Pathway

Adds the direct federal disability-income pathway, covering both SSI and SSDI without confusing their rules.

Income, disability and insured-work requirements differ; decisions and appeals can take time.

Arizona Department of Economic Security - Unemployment Insurance Benefits

Adds wage replacement for eligible people who have recently lost work.

Applicants must meet UI rules and continue required claims and work-search reporting.

GreenPath Financial Wellness - Free Credit, Debt and Housing Counseling

Offers remote debt and budget counseling when a client needs a manageable financial plan.

Counseling is not a cash grant; optional plans or specialized services may have fees.

Azura / Mesa United Way - Volunteer Income Tax Assistance (VITA)

Adds free local tax preparation that can help eligible households claim refunds and credits.

Schedules and return scope vary; confirm the currently published summer or next-season arrangement.

Community Legal Services - Public Benefits Legal Assistance

Adds legal help when a public benefit has been denied, reduced or terminated.

Intake, financial eligibility, legal scope and representation capacity apply.

Banner Health - Arizona Financial Assistance Program for Discounted and Charity Care

Adds a medical-bill relief pathway that can matter even when ordinary rent or utility programs cannot help.

It applies to eligible Banner bills; the applicable policy and financial review determine any reduction.

Disabled American Veterans Chapter 8 - Veteran Financial Assistance Grant

Adds a local veteran emergency grant with concrete Mesa intake and small covered-expense limits.

The grant is limited to eligible veterans, up to $300, with proof that any remaining balance can be paid.

Control Alt Delete - One-Time Emergency Escape Assistance

Adds an advocate-referred route for immediate practical barriers to escaping domestic violence.

A qualified advocate must request help; survivors cannot self-apply and assistance depends on funds and scope.

Gaps: The set does not cover every circumstance: caregiver costs, refugee-specific aid, matched savings, funeral costs, home or vehicle repairs, disease-specific funds and city/provider-specific bill discounts remain in the explained reserve. Geographic and eligibility exclusions mean no single resource fits every client.

Reentry Support

Nine distinct providers cover local clinical and employment access, record barriers, men’s and women’s housing, veteran and youth pathways, recovery treatment and practical-expense help for a group often excluded elsewhere. Different providers and eligibility routes spread referrals; more specialized alternatives remain in the reserve.

Confirm coverage, costs and appointment availability; this is not immediate housing.

Homeless Services

Ten complementary routes cover local outreach, family and adult shelter assessment, daytime survival needs, youth and veteran pathways, single-women shelter and medical respite, spreading referrals among several agencies.

Starter set

City of Mesa Office of Homeless Solutions - Homeless Resource Line (HOPE Line)

Provides a Mesa outreach entry point for people living outside and those needing help reaching shelter.

Outreach response and shelter placement are not immediate guarantees.

Family Housing Hub - Coordinated Entry for Families Experiencing Homelessness

Provides the coordinated-entry route for families with children, including a directed Mesa assessment option.

Assessment does not guarantee a family shelter vacancy; use the current 211 intake route.

A New Leaf - East Valley Men's Center

Adds an emergency shelter pathway for adult men in Mesa.

Prescreening and capacity apply; children cannot stay on site.

Christ Church / City Hope Arizona - Mesa Day Respite Center and City Hope Mesa Center

Adds a local daytime place to cool down and connect with practical support.

Seasonal hours and individual services vary; it is not overnight shelter.

Paz de Cristo Community Center - Meals, Basic Needs and Empowerment

Provides daily meals and scheduled hygiene, mail and document help in downtown Mesa.

Different services have different schedules and limits; it is not a shelter.

Keys to Change - Brian Garcia Welcome Center / Key Campus Single-Adult Coordinated Entry

Adds the Phoenix campus entry point for single-adult assessment and connected services.

Travel may be needed; each partner has its own hours and eligibility.

Native American Connections - HomeBase Youth Emergency Shelter and Youth Housing Services

Adds dedicated young-adult shelter and drop-in access, with a wider age range for youth housing assessment.

Shelter ages 18-24 differ from assessment ages 18-26, and beds require screening.

Phoenix VA Health Care System - Community Resource and Referral Center (CRRC) / Homeless Veteran Care

Provides a federal veteran-specific assessment and housing-support route.

Veteran and programme eligibility apply; clinical and housing benefits are not automatic.

UMOM New Day Centers - Halle Women's Center

Adds a distinct shelter programme for single women.

Intake, referral and current capacity need confirmation; this is separate from family housing assessment.

Circle the City - Medical Respite, Mobile Medical Care and Street Medicine

Adds medical outreach and recuperative care for people whose homelessness is complicated by health needs.

Respite admission depends on clinical criteria and referral; it is not ordinary walk-up shelter.

Gaps: Dedicated DV escape, pets, legal barriers, transitional family housing, employment-linked housing and specialized tribal or HIV support remain important reserves. No starter promises an available bed, immediate placement or universally eligible housing assistance.

ID Recovery

Combine distinct local help with official issuers, record correction, immigration/consular needs and an interstate record finder. Multiple assistance providers spread referrals and offer alternatives when schedules or eligibility do not fit.

Starter set

Homeless ID Project - Mesa and Phoenix replacement ID services

Provides specialized help rebuilding missing identity documents, with a scheduled Mesa clinic and a broader Phoenix network.

Clinic schedules, document requirements and available funding apply; it does not issue government credentials.

Adds a separate Mesa provider for adult ID vouchers, birth-certificate paperwork and receiving mail.

Tuesday vouchers are limited; birth-certificate assistance requires a hard-copy state ID.

Provides the official Arizona ID and replacement-credential process, including applicable fee exceptions.

Applicants still need the required identity and residency evidence; homelessness alone does not create a general fee waiver.

Maricopa County Department of Public Health - Office of Vital Registration East Valley office

Provides the local official route to certified Arizona birth and death records.

Restricted-record eligibility applies; notarization does not guarantee service without acceptable identity evidence.

Proof and appointment/card-center rules apply; cards are mailed after a completed request.

This is legal information, not guaranteed attorney representation; issuing agencies must be updated separately.

Confirm the specific form and fee; the clinic does not handle asylum or immigration-court cases.

Mexican nationality and service-specific proof, appointment and fee rules apply.

The CDC directory does not issue records or pay fees; the selected jurisdiction sets its requirements.

Gaps: Tribal, military, school, foster-care, reentry, survivor and gender-affirming needs are covered in the reserve. No starter is a universal solution for a person with no documents at all.

Transportation

Cover everyday transit, disability access, covered and charitable medical rides, flexible ride assistance, local volunteer trips, bicycles, employment travel, vehicle repairs and long-distance care. Distinct nonprofit and public pathways spread referrals beyond a few providers.

Starter set

Valley Metro — Bus, rail, trip planning and fare access

Provides the main bus and rail network for everyday Mesa trips, with route planning and cash or digital fare options.

Route coverage, operating times, transfers and fares need to fit the particular trip; not every address has nearby service.

Valley Metro - ADA Paratransit / East Valley Paratransit

Provides accessible shared rides when a disability prevents someone from using regular buses or rail.

ADA certification, eligible trip addresses and advance reservations are required; age alone does not qualify.

AHCCCS — Non-emergency medical transportation

Opens the medical-transport benefit that can pay for covered care trips through an AHCCCS member’s assigned plan.

Enrollment, covered trip purpose and plan-specific booking rules apply; emergency-only coverage is excluded.

2-1-1 Arizona Transportation Hotline and Ride United essential rides

Provides a broad starting point for essential-ride assistance when the client does not fit a single specialized program.

Free rides depend on current funding and screening; calling does not guarantee a same-day trip.

Aster Aging — Neighbors volunteer support

Adds local volunteer rides for older adults in Mesa, Chandler and Gilbert, including grocery and pharmacy trips.

Enrollment and volunteer availability apply; this is not emergency or guaranteed on-demand transportation.

WE-CYCLE-USA - Community Cycling Center / Earn-a-Bike

Offers a practical bicycle and repair-help alternative for people who can travel safely by bike.

The current shop is in Apache Junction; adults may need to complete work-trade hours, and inventory varies.

The Worker / St. Joseph the Worker - Mesa Employment Services

Connects job seekers with transportation support through an employment office in Mesa.

Help supports an employment plan; ask intake about the specific pass or fuel assistance currently available.

Worthy of Wheels - Transportation Assistance / Vehicle Repair Application

Adds a general Arizona vehicle-assistance application for an essential car the client cannot afford to repair.

Vehicle ownership, insurance, a valid license and financial documentation are required; assistance depends on funding.

American Cancer Society - Road To Recovery

Adds free volunteer rides specifically for cancer appointments, independent of the general Medicaid pathway.

Local driver availability and advance notice are essential; accompanying-caregiver rules can apply.

Angel Flight West - Free Medical Flights and Earth Angels Ground Transportation

Extends the set to long-distance medical care through charitable flights and possible ground connections.

Medical release, trip fit and volunteer availability apply; these flights provide no in-flight medical care.

Gaps: Reduced-fare and RideChoice programs, veteran-specific rides, childcare/foster and enrolled-program transport, driving-document help, rural/tribal routes, additional private accessible providers and roadside help remain in the reserve. No option guarantees capacity or an immediate ride.

Veterans

Combines local navigation, benefits advocacy, medical and counselling access, housing, work, college, financial relief, crisis support and transportation. Several independent providers give practical alternatives while retaining essential VA entry points. These choices are a complementary starting set, not a claim that providers are superior.

Starter set

AZ Veterans Resource Center — case management and family/peer support

Provides a local, face-to-face starting point for several veteran and family needs, with case management and peer support.

The centre connects people to programmes; it does not guarantee a payment, job or housing placement.

Arizona Department of Veterans' Services - Veteran Benefits Counselors

Provides free accredited help with veteran benefits, claims, appeals and discharge-related questions.

Counselling requires an appointment, and the underlying benefit has its own service and eligibility rules.

Staff Sergeant Alexander W. Conrad VA Health Care Clinic

Provides an East Valley VA medical home with primary care and several clinical specialties.

The clinic is in Gilbert; VA eligibility, referrals and appointments apply, and dental benefits have narrower rules.

Mesa Vet Center - Readjustment Counseling and Referral Services

Provides nearby confidential readjustment and family counselling through Mesa Vet Center.

Vet Center eligibility differs from ordinary VA enrollment; this is nonmedical counselling and not emergency care.

National Community Health Partners - Housing for Heroes: Supportive Services for Veteran Families (SSVF)

Adds an independent SSVF provider for veteran housing stabilisation, case management and possible move-in or bill assistance.

Veteran-family, income and housing-status rules apply, and assistance depends on the case plan and available funding.

Workforce Center @ Mesa

Adds a Mesa workforce centre offering veteran priority, job-search help and practical employment supports.

Some training or specialised programmes have additional criteria; the centre cannot guarantee a job or assist with unemployment-insurance applications.

Mesa Community College - Office of Veteran Services / Veteran Resource Center

Adds local college support for using military education benefits, advising and college transition.

Services focus on MCC students and applicants; benefit approval is separate and a Request for Benefits is needed each term.

Arizona Department of Veterans' Services - Arizona Military Family Relief Fund

Adds a state financial-relief option for qualifying military households with service-related hardship.

Deployment, Arizona connection and other eligibility rules are restrictive; approved vendor payments can take 30–45 days.

Veterans Crisis Line

Provides immediate, round-the-clock veteran-specific crisis support by telephone, text or chat without requiring VA enrollment.

This is crisis support and connection to help, not ongoing therapy or guaranteed placement.

Resurrection Street Ministry - Veterans Transportation

Addresses a practical barrier with scheduled rides to veteran medical and service appointments in the East Valley.

Rides require advance arrangements and eligibility screening; capacity and the particular destination must be confirmed.

Gaps: The reserve includes dental assistance outside VA eligibility, discharge-upgrade and court representation, caregiver support, accessible housing and repairs, service dogs, entrepreneurship, women-specific services, peer activities and additional housing or financial providers.
